questions.q: A particle moves in a straight line such that its displacement $s$ meters at time $t$ seconds is given by $s = t^3 - 6t^2 + 9t + 4$. Find the possible values of its acceleration when the velocity is zero.
questions.explain:
Velocity $v = \frac{ds}{dt} = 3t^2 - 12t + 9$.
Set $v = 0$ to find the times when the particle is at rest: $3(t^2 - 4t + 3) = 0 \implies (t-1)(t-3) = 0$. So, $t = 1\text{ s}$ or $t = 3\text{ s}$.
Acceleration $a = \frac{dv}{dt} = 6t - 12$.
At $t = 1$, $a = 6(1) - 12 = -6\text{ m/s}^2$.
At $t = 3$, $a = 6(3) - 12 = 6\text{ m/s}^2$.
The possible values are $\pm 6\text{ m/s}^2$.

questions.q: A car accelerates uniformly from rest at $2\text{ m/s}^2$ for $5\text{ seconds}$. What is its final velocity?
questions.explain:
Using the first equation of motion: $v = u + at$.
Since it starts from rest, $u = 0$. $a = 2\text{ m/s}^2$ and $t = 5\text{ s}$.
$v = 0 + (2 \times 5) = 10\text{ m/s}$.

questions.q: A stone is dropped from a height of $45\text{ m}$. With what velocity does it hit the ground? (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.explain:
Using the equation $v^2 = u^2 + 2gs$ where $u = 0$ (since it is dropped).
$v^2 = 0 + 2(10)(45) = 900$.
$v = \sqrt{900} = 30\text{ m/s}$.

questions.q: A ball of mass $0.2\text{ kg}$ falls vertically and hits a hard floor with a velocity of $10\text{ m/s}$. It rebounds vertically upwards with a velocity of $8\text{ m/s}$. Find the magnitude of the impulse exerted by the floor on the ball.
questions.explain:
Impulse $I = \text{change in momentum} = m(v - u)$.
Taking the upward direction as positive, the final velocity $v = 8\text{ m/s}$ and the initial velocity $u = -10\text{ m/s}$.
$I = 0.2(8 - (-10)) = 0.2(18) = 3.6\text{ N s}$.

questions.q: A constant force acts on a body of mass $5\text{ kg}$, changing its velocity from $10\text{ m/s}$ to $20\text{ m/s}$ in $2\text{ seconds}$. Find the magnitude of the force.
questions.explain:
Acceleration $a = \frac{v - u}{t} = \frac{20 - 10}{2} = \frac{10}{2} = 5\text{ m/s}^2$.
Force $F = ma = 5 \times 5 = 25\text{ N}$.

questions.q: A particle of mass $2\text{ kg}$ is moving with a constant velocity of $(3\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j})\text{ m/s}$. Find the magnitude of its momentum.
questions.explain:
First, find the magnitude of velocity: $|\mathbf{v}| = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{9 + 16} = \sqrt{25} = 5\text{ m/s}$.
Momentum $p = m|\mathbf{v}| = 2 \times 5 = 10\text{ kg m/s}$.

questions.q: A particle starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at $4\text{ m/s}^2$ for $6\text{ seconds}$. Find the total distance covered during this time.
questions.explain:
Using the equation of motion $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$.
Since it starts from rest, $u = 0$, $a = 4\text{ m/s}^2$, and $t = 6\text{ s}$.
$s = 0 + \frac{1}{2}(4)(6^2) = 2(36) = 72\text{ m}$.

questions.q: A constant force of $50\text{ N}$ acts on a body of mass $2\text{ kg}$ for $0.1\text{ seconds}$. Calculate the change in velocity of the body.
questions.explain:
Impulse = Force $\times$ Time = Change in momentum.
$F \Delta t = m \Delta v \implies 50 \times 0.1 = 2 \times \Delta v \implies 5 = 2\Delta v \implies \Delta v = 2.5\text{ m/s}$.

questions.q: A train travelling at $72\text{ km/h}$ is brought to rest uniformly in $20\text{ seconds}$. Find the magnitude of its retardation.
questions.explain:
First convert velocity to m/s: $72\text{ km/h} = 72 \times \frac{5}{18} = 20\text{ m/s}$.
Using $v = u + at \implies 0 = 20 + a(20) \implies 20a = -20 \implies a = -1\text{ m/s}^2$.
The magnitude of retardation is $1\text{ m/s}^2$.

questions.q: The velocity of a particle $t$ seconds after starting from a fixed origin $O$ is given by $v = (4t - t^2)\text{ m/s}$. Find its displacement from $O$ after $3\text{ seconds}$.
questions.explain:
Displacement $s$ is the integral of velocity $v$ with respect to time: $s = \int (4t - t^2) \, dt = 2t^2 - \frac{t^3}{3} + C$.
Since it starts at $O$, $s=0$ when $t=0$, meaning $C=0$.
At $t = 3$, $s = 2(3^2) - \frac{3^3}{3} = 2(9) - \frac{27}{3} = 18 - 9 = 9\text{ m}$.

questions.q: A particle moves with a constant velocity of $(4\mathbf{i} - 3\mathbf{j})\text{ m/s}$. If it is initially at a position $(2\mathbf{i} + 5\mathbf{j})\text{ m}$, what is its position vector after $5\text{ seconds}$?
questions.explain:
The position vector is given by $\mathbf{r} = \mathbf{r}_0 + \mathbf{v}t$.
$\mathbf{r} = (2\mathbf{i} + 5\mathbf{j}) + 5(4\mathbf{i} - 3\mathbf{j}) = (2\mathbf{i} + 5\mathbf{j}) + (20\mathbf{i} - 15\mathbf{j}) = 22\mathbf{i} - 10\mathbf{j}$.
